Closed forms for the constants in the odd-weight identities
between dihedral modular graph functions
Noah Schittenhelm
Hack-Nation 2026, Team Ninja Turtles
Preprint, October 2026

Abstract We study the combinations Xw of dihedral
modular graph functions C(a, b, c) of odd weight w
introduced by D’Hoker, Green and Vanhove, whose
Laplacian is proportional to the Eisenstein series E(w).
For the odd weights 3 ≤ w ≤ 61 we show Xw =
fw E(w) + gw ζ(w) with fw = 3((w − 1)/2)!/w and
gw = 6|Bw−1 |/((w − 1)/2)!. The proof has three steps.
The Laplace equation is derived in exact rational algebra.
Harmonicity, invariance and polynomial growth force
Xw − fw E(w) to be constant. The constant is read off
from a Laurent polynomial evaluated in rational arithmetic. The space of combinations with ∆X ∈ QE(w)
is shown exactly to be one-dimensional for odd w and
zero for even w, for 3 ≤ w ≤ 25. Independently of the
proof, the verifier confirmed the constants numerically
at w = 3, . . . , 17. The full weight-11 basis carries exactly one relation. The statement for all odd w is a
conjecture. The proof rests on two assumptions not
checked by code, a published theorem and a standard
lemma.

Numerical identification of the constants by integerrelation search is therefore fragile.
We prove closed forms for fw and gw by an exact
route, and confirm them by independent numerics.
Summary of results.
• Theorem 1 shows Xw = fw E(w) + gw ζ(w) with
closed forms for fw , gw , for the odd weights 3 ≤
w ≤ 61 (exact Laplace algebra plus a rational
Laurent computation).
• Theorem 2 shows that the space of combinations
X with ∆X ∈ QE(w) is one-dimensional for odd
w and zero for even w, for 3 ≤ w ≤ 25 (exact).
• Conjecture 1 extends the closed forms beyond the
proved range w ≤ 61; it was read off from w =
3, . . . , 13 before the proof.
• The supporting propositions and numerical observations record independent confirmation at w =
3, . . . , 17, the full weight-11 relation space, and a
hardening run.

Genus-one string amplitudes · Computer-assisted proof

1 Introduction
Dihedral modular graph functions C(a, b, c) arise as coefficients in the low-energy expansion of the one-loop
closed-string amplitude. They satisfy Laplace eigenvalue equations with inhomogeneous terms that are
polynomial in non-holomorphic Eisenstein series [1]. At
each odd weight there is a combination Xw with Laplace
eigenvalue zero, up to a term proportional to E(w). Its
multiplicity is one for each odd weight and zero for each
even weight [1].
D’Hoker, Green and Vanhove determine such identities up to additive constants of integration, which are
fixed by the behaviour near the cusp [1]. The constants
g7 , g9 are left undetermined there, while g7 appears explicitly in a later work [2]. The Laurent polynomial of
each C(a, b, c) is known in closed form from D’Hoker
and Kaidi. The open question is the value of fw and
gw at larger odd w.
This is hard because the number of functions C(a, b, c)
grows with w, and the constant is a Laurent term of a
long combination. At w = 17 the identity involves eight
functions, with a leading integer coefficient 51819264000.

Proof. The argument has three steps, following.
1. Exact rational computation in the algebraic Laplace
representation gives ∆Xw = w(w − 1)fw E(w) with
no other terms. Since ∆E(w) = w(w − 1)E(w), it
follows that ∆(Xw − fw E(w)) = 0.
2. Xw − fw E(w) is harmonic, modular invariant and
of polynomial growth at the cusp, hence constant.
3. The constant equals the τ20 term of its Laurent
polynomial. This polynomial was computed in
rational arithmetic from Proposition 2.1 and Theorem 5.1 of D’Hoker–Kaidi, with the transcription
checked against their eq. 5.19. The terms not involving products of zeta values agree with those of
fw E(w) + gw ζ(w), which serves as a consistency
check, and the constant term equals gw ζ(w).

5 Discussion
The identities express, for odd w, the combination Xw
of two-loop graphs through a single Eisenstein series
plus a single zeta value, with rational constants of closed
form. The exact route avoids numerical integer-relation
searches, whose coefficient height is the main obstruction at large w (cf.). The numerical observations are
independent confirmation, not part of the proof.
Limitations. Theorem 1 is conditional on the correctness of Theorem 5.1 of D’Hoker–Kaidi and on the standard lemma used in step 2. Both are cited, not checked
